result.detail: Design choices: (1) The only assumption is assume(!rst_n) in the first cycle, which spec 3.1 justifies. take and give are left fully free, including both high at once, so there is no over-constraint. (2) All assertions are immediate and procedural, each inside if guards with no implication operator, so formal.cover can derive a guard cover for each one. (3) Assertions read ports only (credits, avail, full, err) and do not restate RTL internals. (4) err-only-on-refusal is an extra assertion, drawn from the err port description, so a mutant that sets err spuriously fails. (5) Limitation of CC-PARAM: MAX=255 and other large values are not instantiated, because their underflow guards would need about 256 cycles and the cover check uses the same depth of 20. The result therefore covers MAX in {1,3,4}, which includes the MAX=1 corner where zero and full are adjacent and a value that is not a power of two. A wider sweep, or a separate deep bmc/cover job for MAX=255, would need a second setup, which this single-formal_spec task does not allow.
